observations: Photo is extremely dark/underexposed, taken indoors with minimal light.
Shape shows a bulky curved-back unit consistent with a CRT (tube) television, including visible vents and a rounded rear cone.
No screen face, brand logo, model plate, or power cable/plug clearly visible.
Item sits on a tiled floor; no power-on state, no visible damage marks, no screen cracks visible due to darkness and angle.

claims.evidence: No brand logo, model label, or screen visible in photo 0; size cannot be measured or confirmed from the image.

claims.claim: Transformer blown (implying unit does not power on / is faulty)
claims.evidence: No internal view, no power-on test, no visible burn marks or damage shown in photo 0.

risks.risk: Unconfirmed brand/model — cannot verify it is genuinely LG or 29-inch.
risks.proof: Clear, well-lit photo of the brand label/model sticker on the back or front bezel.
risks.if_unproven: priced as a generic unbranded/unverified CRT TV of unknown size

risks.risk: Unit confirmed non-working per seller's own description (blown transformer), extent of damage unknown (could affect more than transformer, e.g., tube, board).
risks.proof: Video of attempted power-on, plus a photo of the opened back showing the transformer/board damage.
risks.if_unproven: priced as fully non-working, parts/scrap value only

risks.risk: Physical condition of screen/tube (cracks, scratches) cannot be assessed due to darkness.
risks.proof: Well-lit photo of the full front screen and all sides.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming possible additional cosmetic/screen damage

risks.risk: Completeness of unit — remote, stand, cables not shown.
risks.proof: Photo showing accessories included in the sale.
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare unit only, no accessories

proof_requests: A clear, well-lit photo of the back panel showing the brand/model sticker.
A photo of the full front screen in good lighting.
A video attempting to power the TV on (even if it fails, to confirm the exact symptom).
A photo of the open back showing the blown transformer/board for damage assessment.
A photo with a tape measure across the screen to confirm the claimed 29-inch size.
response.reason: The silhouette in the dark photo is consistent with a CRT-style television, enough to price by type, but brand, size, and the extent of the seller-claimed transformer fault are all unverified, so it must be priced at worst case as a non-working, unbranded CRT TV until better photos are provided.
